claims.text: A request travels forward through Kestrel, routing, and each registered middleware in order, reaching the endpoint only if nothing short-circuits first.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Middleware fundamentals and Routing fundamentals

claims.text: Once the endpoint or a short-circuit produces a response, control returns back out through every middleware that ran on the way in, in the reverse of the order they ran in. Kestrel is what turns the response into bytes for the client.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Middleware fundamentals (middleware order / write custom middleware)

claims.text: A middleware registered before the one that short-circuits still runs its own after-next code on the way back out, because from its own view next simply returned.

OrdersController.Get(int id) has no [Authorize] attribute, so UseAuthorization lets a GET with no Authorization header through to it; it returns 404 via NotFound() when no order with the given id is found.

curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/999999 (nonexistent order) to the stage-1 example system prints the status code and headers, 404; docker compose logs api (the service running DonHang.Api is named api) prints a RequestLoggingMiddleware line reporting 404.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang stage-1 lab: docker compose logs api after curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/999999

claims.text: In DonHang.Api/Program.cs, the forward order of wiring calls is ExceptionHandlingMiddleware, RequestLoggingMiddleware, UseCors, UseAuthentication, UseAuthorization, MapControllers; for a request the endpoint or UseAuthorization answers, the reverse order is the same list backward.

POST /api/v1/orders with no Authorization header to the stage-1 lab gets 401 from UseAuthorization itself, not passed on to the endpoint; docker compose logs api shows a RequestLoggingMiddleware line for it reporting 401.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang stage-1 lab: docker compose logs api after curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders

claims.text: The app.Run() call at the end of Program.cs runs the app, starting the server that then listens for connections, and blocks the calling thread until the app shuts down.

With only the JWT bearer scheme registered, as in DonHang.Api, UseAuthentication does not reject a request that has no token; of the pair, UseAuthorization is the one that answers with 401 instead of passing the request on.
ExceptionHandlingMiddleware's InvokeAsync has no code after its try/catch around next(context); when no exception is thrown, nothing runs after next returns.
